place.title: Place {ref} (thermistor)
place.text: Push the thermistor {ref}'s 2 thin legs into column f: one into hole {hole.a}, the other into {hole.b}. The small black bead is the part that measures.
place.tip: A thermistor has no + or −. Its legs are thin: push them in close to the breadboard so they don't bend.

why: {ref} is a thermistor: its resistance drops as it gets warmer (10 kΩ at 25 °C). With the 10 kΩ resistor below it, it makes a voltage divider, so the code can work out the temperature from the voltage between them.

wire.ground: This connects the bottom of the divider (the 10 kΩ resistor) to ground.
wire.power: This puts 3.3 V on {ref}'s top leg, the top of the divider.
wire.adc: {pin} is an analog input (ADC): it measures the voltage between {ref} and the 10 kΩ resistor (0 to 65535); it rises as {ref} warms up, and the code turns it into °C.
